title: Fppf sheafification preserves affine limit continuity
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $F:(\mathit{Sch}/B)_{fppf}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathit{Sets}$ be a presheaf on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. Suppose that for every small nonempty directed set $I$ and every inverse system of affine $B$-schemes $(T_i)$ with limit $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_iF(T_i)\to F(T)$ is bijective. Let $F^{\#}$ be its set-valued fppf sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Then for every such inverse system the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_iF^{\#}(T_i)\longrightarrow F^{\#}(T)$$
is bijective. All colimits here are filtered colimits of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No sheaf condition on $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $G^+$ for the plus construction of any presheaf $G$. Its sections are classes $[\mathcal V,s]$ of matching families; two classes agree precisely after restriction to a common covering refinement. These are the representation, equality and restriction assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf]. For an affine base, [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement] permits both the representing cover and any cover witnessing equality to be replaced by a finite affine fppf cover. Such a cover is standard in the explicit sense of [lem-sfb-standard-fppf-cover-limit-descent]. We will prove continuity for $G^+$ whenever $G$ satisfies the continuity hypothesis of the item.

Fix a standard covering $\mathcal V_i=\{V_{i,a}\to T_i\}_{a=1}^m$, and for $j\ge i$ put $V_{j,a}=V_{i,a}\times_{T_i}T_j$, $V_a=V_{i,a}\times_{T_i}T$. Base change preserves the covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. All $V_{j,a}$ and $V_{j,a}\times_{T_j}V_{j,b}$ are affine: maps between affines are affine, and affine morphisms remain affine under base change and have affine source over an affine target. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] to $V_{i,a}$ and to $V_{i,a}\times_{T_i}V_{i,b}$; the fibre-product universal property identifies their limits with $V_a$ and $V_a\times_TV_b$. Thus the hypothesis on $G$ applies to both systems. We also use that tails of $I$ suffice: every index has a common upper bound with $i$, and the element/equality criterion for filtered set colimits gives the same colimit on $I_{\ge i}$.

For this fixed cover the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{j\ge i}H^0(\mathcal V_j,G)\to H^0(\mathcal V,G)$ is bijective. Indeed, lift each of the finitely many components $s_a\in G(V_a)$ to a stage using continuity on the first systems of step 2. Choose a common stage for these lifts. Each of the finitely many matching equations holds at the limit on $V_a\times_TV_b$; continuity on the second systems and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise](3) give a later stage where all those equations hold. This proves surjectivity. If two matching families have the same limit, apply the same eventual-equality criterion to their finitely many components and choose a common later stage; this proves injectivity. The description of $H^0$ used here is exactly [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction](a). When $m=0$ the matching set is a singleton at every stage and the argument still holds.

For surjectivity of $\operatorname{colim}_iG^+(T_i)\to G^+(T)$ take $x\in G^+(T)$ and choose a matching family on a finite affine fppf cover as in step 1. By [lem-sfb-standard-fppf-cover-limit-descent] this cover is the base change of a standard cover at some stage $i$. Step 3 lifts its matching family to some $j\ge i$. Its class in $G^+(T_j)$ restricts to $x$, by the restriction formula of [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf](3).

For injectivity represent two colimit elements at a common stage $i$, using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], and represent their plus sections by matching families on standard covers $\mathcal V_i,\mathcal V_i^\prime$ (step 1). If their limit sections coincide, [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf](2) and affine refinement give a standard cover $\mathcal W$ of $T$ with refinement maps to both limit covers, on which the two families agree. Descend $\mathcal W$ by [lem-sfb-standard-fppf-cover-limit-descent], and pass to a common stage $k\ge i$. Descend its finitely many component maps to the two covers by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-arrows-descent], retaining their finite index assignments. The hypotheses hold: all component schemes and bases are affine, hence qcqs, the cover components are finitely presented over their bases, and finite presentation is preserved by base change [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Maps between affine bases are affine. Thus the descended arrows are morphisms of coverings over $T_k$. The pulled-back families are matching families on $\mathcal W_k$ whose limit families coincide. Step 3 gives their equality at a later stage. Their plus classes are therefore equal by [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf](2), proving injectivity. All refinements and section maps are the actual descended maps, so this equality identifies the canonical colimit elements.

Steps 2--5 prove the asserted continuity for $G^+$ for every presheaf $G$ satisfying the hypothesis, without separatedness or a sheaf assumption. Apply them first to $G=F$ and then to $G=F^+$. The resulting continuity for $F^{++}$ is the desired continuity for $F^\#$: [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-theorem](3) gives an isomorphism of presheaves $F^{++}\simeq F^\#$ carrying the sheafification unit to the given unit. Its naturality with respect to every $T\to T_i$ makes the two canonical comparison maps commute with these bijections, and hence transfers bijectivity.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q49-76fa2e5d8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks Tag 049O (spaces-limits.tex, lemma-sheafify-finite-presentation) and its proof in full. The statement matches the source hypothesis for hypothesis (affine directed limits, set-valued presheaf, arbitrary base) and is unchanged, as are the stmt_deps; the parent's step 4 uses it as stated. There are no new nodes, and proof_deps equals the union of the uses. Step by step: (1) the plus-presheaf node's clauses (1)-(3) and 021P give standard (021Q) representing covers and standard equality covers at T and at each T_i. (2) The 021O(3) Mathlib leaf, 01SH and the affine permanence lemma make every component and overlap affine; 01YZ identifies the component and overlap limits, and the tail I_{>=i} is a valid small directed set. (3) The fixed-cover H^0 bijection is written out over finitely many components and equations with eventual equality, including m=0. (4) Surjectivity uses 049N(1) cover descent and restriction clause (3). (5) Injectivity descends the equality cover W by 049N(1) and its finitely many component maps by 01ZM(2), whose hypotheses I checked: affine so qcqs, fp preserved by base change. Step 3 then gives equality at a later stage, and criterion (2) gives equality of the classes. This replaces the source's colimit interchange without any cofinality assumption. (6) The plus-plus theorem (3) gives F^{++} isomorphic to F^# as presheaves compatibly with the units, which transfers bijectivity. Edge cases checked: empty T and the empty cover, constant systems, non-injective transitions, non-affine B. No duplicate: the rg search for 049O and sheafification/continuity hits only the item and its parent, plus different-variable results. I accept all declared tool_uses as generic inputs of Tag 049O. Batch 5: lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change is a Mathlib leaf for Stacks 021O(3), a basic property of the fppf topology, outside both the trace-formula and the Poincare-duality assumptions and their proofs, so the citation is acceptable.
